dedupe_keys.name: study on implementation and monitoring of the broadband cost reduction directive european commission 2018

description: The European Commission published this study on the implementation and monitoring of the Broadband Cost Reduction Directive (2014/61/EU), which aims to cut the cost of deploying fast broadband by facilitating shared use and coordinated deployment of physical infrastructure such as ducts and poles across electronic communications, energy, transport and water. The study defines a monitoring methodology, gathers data to assess the status of implementation and change in outcomes since the application date in July 2016, and identifies best-practice examples of access and co-deployment regimes and standards for in-building infrastructure, based on case studies and interviews. Findings on the page: little time had passed since national transposition, so no definitive conclusions on the effect on deployment cost yet; operators report improved access to physical and in-building infrastructure and to information about it, but limited progress on coordination of civil works, easing civil works permits and access to buildings. Producer: the European Commission, published 27 June 2018. Coverage: EU member states. Access: the report is linked from the library page. Licence and cost: free; no licence text read. Caveats: the study is from 2018 and its survey findings are early, opinion-based results. Simulation uses: it provides evidence for infrastructure sharing and duct access assumptions in broadband roll-out and capacity-planning models. Related record: the ITU broadband maps of terrestrial transmission networks (data-itu-broadband-maps-terrestrial-transmission).
